title: Greek Salad (Horiatiki)
description: The classic village salad of Cyprus and Greece — ripe tomatoes, cool cucumber, sharp feta, and a drizzle of good olive oil. No lettuce, no frills.
instructions: Cut tomatoes into large wedges and place in a wide salad bowl.
Peel cucumber if desired, cut in half lengthwise, then slice into thick half-moons. Add to bowl.
Slice red onion into thin rings and add to bowl along with sliced green bell pepper and olives.
Place the block of feta on top. Drizzle generously with olive oil, sprinkle with oregano, salt, and pepper.
Serve immediately — the feta is meant to be broken at the table, not pre-crumbled.

title: Halloumi Toast
description: Pan-fried halloumi on thick sourdough with bursting cherry tomatoes and fresh basil. Simple, fast, and deeply satisfying.
instructions: Slice halloumi into 8 slabs about 5mm thick. Pat dry with kitchen paper.
Toast the sourdough slices.
Heat olive oil in a non-stick pan over medium-high heat. Add halloumi and cook 2 minutes per side until golden.
In the same pan, add cherry tomatoes and cook 1–2 minutes until just starting to burst.
Place 2 halloumi slabs on each toast, top with tomatoes, fresh basil, and a crack of black pepper.

title: Scrambled Eggs with Fresh Herbs
description: Slow-cooked, creamy scrambled eggs finished with fresh chives and parsley. The technique — low heat, constant stirring — makes all the difference.
instructions: Crack eggs into a bowl, add milk, salt, and pepper. Whisk well.
Melt butter in a non-stick pan over the lowest heat setting.
Add eggs. Stir constantly with a spatula, pulling the curds slowly across the pan. This should take 4–5 minutes.
Remove from heat while eggs look slightly underdone — residual heat finishes them.
Fold in chives and parsley. Serve immediately.

title: Pasta Aglio e Olio
description: The midnight pasta of Naples — spaghetti, garlic, chili, and your best olive oil. Nothing more, and nothing less.
instructions: Boil salted water and cook spaghetti until al dente. Reserve 1 cup of pasta water before draining.
While pasta cooks, thinly slice the garlic.
Warm olive oil in a large pan over medium-low heat. Add garlic and chili flakes. Cook gently for 4–5 minutes until garlic turns golden — don't let it burn.
Add drained pasta to the pan with a splash of pasta water. Toss vigorously to emulsify.
Remove from heat, add parsley, and toss again. Serve with parmesan if using.

title: Hummus with Warm Pita
description: Silky, lemony homemade hummus — better than any shop-bought tub. The secret is blending the chickpeas while still warm and using plenty of tahini.
instructions: Drain and rinse chickpeas. Warm them briefly in a small pot of water — warm chickpeas blend much smoother.
Add chickpeas, tahini, lemon juice, garlic, cumin, salt, and 3 tbsp cold water to a food processor.
Blend for 3–4 minutes until ultra-smooth, scraping down the sides. Adjust salt and lemon to taste.
Warm pita bread in a dry pan for 1 minute per side or directly on a gas flame.
Serve hummus in a bowl, drizzle with olive oil, and dust with paprika.

title: Avocado Toast with Feta
description: Creamy avocado on sourdough, lifted with lemon, contrasted with salty feta and a pinch of chili. Ready in 8 minutes.
instructions: Toast the sourdough slices until golden.
Halve and pit the avocados. Scoop flesh into a bowl, add lemon juice, salt, and pepper. Mash with a fork to your preferred texture.
Spread avocado on toast, top with crumbled feta and a pinch of chili flakes.
Serve immediately.

title: Halloumi Saganaki with Honey & Thyme
description: Pan-fried halloumi that's crisp outside and soft within, finished with a drizzle of thyme honey and a squeeze of lemon. A Cypriot taverna staple.
instructions: Slice halloumi into pieces about 1cm thick. Pat dry with paper towels.
Dust each piece lightly with flour, shaking off any excess.
Heat olive oil in a non-stick pan over medium-high heat.
Fry halloumi 2–3 minutes per side until deep golden brown.
Transfer to a serving plate. Drizzle immediately with honey, scatter thyme leaves over the top, and squeeze lemon juice. Finish with black pepper.
Serve at once — halloumi toughens as it cools.

title: Chicken Souvlaki with Pita & Tzatziki
description: Marinated chicken skewers grilled until charred, served in warm pita with cool, garlicky tzatziki. The quintessential Cypriot street food.
instructions: Cut chicken into 3cm cubes. Mix olive oil, juice of 1 lemon, minced garlic, oregano, thyme, salt, and pepper. Toss chicken in marinade and rest for at least 15 minutes (or overnight).
Make tzatziki: grate the cucumber, squeeze out excess water, mix with yogurt, 1 minced garlic clove, dill, a squeeze of lemon, and salt to taste. Refrigerate.
Thread chicken onto skewers (metal or soaked wooden).
Grill over high heat or cook in a ridged grill pan for 5–6 minutes per side until nicely charred and cooked through.
Warm pita breads briefly on the grill or in a dry pan.
Serve skewers in pita with tzatziki and any remaining lemon wedges.

title: Shakshuka
description: Eggs poached directly in a spiced tomato and pepper sauce — one pan, bold flavour, deeply satisfying at any meal.
instructions: Heat olive oil in a large, deep frying pan over medium heat. Add diced onion and cook 5 minutes until softened.
Add sliced red bell peppers and cook another 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic, cumin, paprika, and cayenne. Stir and cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in canned tomatoes, crushing them with a spoon. Season with salt and pepper. Simmer 10 minutes until sauce thickens.
Make 6 wells in the sauce with a spoon and crack an egg into each well.
Cover the pan and cook 5–7 minutes — whites should be set, yolks still runny.
Scatter with parsley and crumbled feta. Serve directly from the pan with crusty bread.

title: Pasta Carbonara
description: Rome's most famous pasta — guanciale, egg yolks, and aged pecorino or parmesan. No cream. Technique is everything here.
instructions: Cook spaghetti in well-salted boiling water until al dente. Reserve 2 cups pasta water.
Meanwhile, cut guanciale into lardons (small cubes). Cook in a dry pan over medium heat until crispy and fat has rendered. Remove pan from heat.
In a bowl, whisk together 4 whole eggs, 2 extra yolks, and grated parmesan. Season with black pepper.
Drain pasta (keeping reserved water). Add hot pasta to the pan with guanciale, off the heat.

Pour egg mixture over pasta, add a splash of pasta water, and toss constantly — the heat from the pasta cooks the eggs. Add more water as needed to achieve a creamy, silky sauce. Never put the pan back on direct heat.
Serve immediately topped with extra parmesan and black pepper.

title: Fakes — Greek Lentil Soup
possibleAdditions: A splash of red wine vinegar
description: A humble, warming lentil soup that's a Greek household staple. The splash of red wine vinegar at the end is non-negotiable.
instructions: Rinse lentils well. Pick over for any stones.
Heat olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Soften diced onion for 5 minutes, then add minced garlic and cook 1 more minute.
Add lentils, canned tomatoes, bay leaves, oregano, and enough water to cover by 5cm. Bring to a boil.
Reduce heat and simmer 30–35 minutes until lentils are tender but not mushy. Add water if it thickens too much.
Remove bay leaves. Season generously with salt and pepper. Stir in red wine vinegar just before serving.

title: Stuffed Mushrooms with Feta & Spinach
description: Large portobello mushrooms filled with wilted spinach, garlic, and crumbled feta, then baked until golden. Great as a starter or light main.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Remove mushroom stalks and chop them finely.
Heat 1 tbsp olive oil in a pan. Cook chopped stalks with minced garlic 3 minutes. Add spinach and cook until wilted, about 2 minutes. Season with salt and pepper.
Transfer spinach mixture to a bowl. Crumble in feta and mix gently.
Place mushroom caps gill-side up on a baking tray. Brush with remaining olive oil.
Fill each cap generously with the spinach-feta mixture. Scatter thyme leaves on top.
Bake 18–20 minutes until mushrooms are tender and the filling is golden.

title: Moussaka
possibleAdditions: Extra cinnamon in the meat sauce
description: The great baked dish of the Greek table — layered aubergine, spiced beef ragù, and a thick béchamel. Effort rewarded with flavour that improves overnight.
instructions: Slice eggplant lengthways into 1cm slabs. Salt generously and leave 20 minutes to draw out moisture. Rinse and pat dry.
Brush eggplant with oil and grill or roast at 220°C until golden, about 15 minutes. Set aside.

Make the meat sauce: cook diced onion in oil 5 minutes. Add garlic then mince. Cook until browned, then add wine, canned tomatoes, tomato paste, cinnamon, and allspice. Simmer 20 minutes until thick. Season well.

Make béchamel: melt butter over medium heat, whisk in flour and cook 1 minute. Gradually add warm milk, whisking constantly until thickened (5–7 minutes). Season with salt, nutmeg, and pepper. Off heat, whisk in eggs and half the parmesan.
Preheat oven to 180°C. Grease a 30×20cm baking dish and dust with breadcrumbs.
Layer half the eggplant, then all the meat sauce, then remaining eggplant.
Pour béchamel over the top. Spread to the edges and sprinkle remaining parmesan.
Bake 45–50 minutes until deep golden on top. Rest 15 minutes before cutting.

title: Kleftiko — Slow-Roasted Lamb
description: Lamb sealed with garlic, herbs and wine in parchment, then slow-roasted until it falls from the bone. Named after the 'kleftes' — outlaws who cooked meat buried in the ground to avoid detection.
instructions: Score the lamb deeply with a knife and push garlic slivers into each cut.
Mix olive oil, lemon juice, oregano, salt, and pepper. Rub all over the lamb. Marinate at least 1 hour, ideally overnight.
Preheat oven to 160°C. Cut potatoes into large wedges and slice tomatoes thickly.
Lay two large sheets of baking parchment (or foil) in a roasting tin, forming a cross. Place lamb on top.
Arrange potatoes and tomatoes around the lamb. Pour over the red wine and any remaining marinade. Tuck in bay leaves, thyme, and rosemary.
Fold the parchment tightly over to seal completely — no steam should escape.
Roast for 3.5–4 hours until the lamb is completely tender and falling off the bone.
Open the parcel for the last 20 minutes to brown the top.

title: Spanakopita — Spinach & Feta Pie
description: Shatteringly crisp phyllo encasing a rich filling of spinach, feta, and dill. A labour of love with layers that snap satisfyingly at the table.
instructions: Cook spinach in batches in a dry pan until wilted. Squeeze out as much water as possible — this is critical. Chop roughly.
Soften diced onion in olive oil for 8 minutes. Cool slightly.
In a large bowl, combine spinach, onion, crumbled feta, beaten eggs, dill, nutmeg, salt, and pepper. Mix well.
Preheat oven to 180°C. Brush a 30×20cm baking dish with butter.
Lay phyllo sheets in the dish, brushing each with melted butter, using half the sheets for the base. Let the sheets overhang the sides.
Spread the spinach-feta filling evenly.
Fold the overhanging phyllo over the filling, then layer the remaining sheets on top, brushing each with butter. Score the top into portions with a sharp knife.
Bake 45–50 minutes until deeply golden and crisp. Rest 10 minutes before cutting.

title: Pastitsio — Greek Pasta Bake
description: Cyprus's answer to lasagne — tubes of pasta layered with spiced beef ragù and a deep béchamel. The cinnamon-scented meat sauce is what sets it apart from its Italian cousin.
instructions: Cook penne until just al dente. Drain and set aside.
Make meat sauce: brown mince in batches in olive oil. Add diced onion and garlic. Pour in wine and let it bubble 2 minutes.
Add canned tomatoes, tomato paste, cinnamon, cloves, salt, and pepper. Simmer 25 minutes until thick.

Make béchamel: melt butter, whisk in flour for 1 minute, then gradually add warm milk. Stir until thickened (7–8 minutes). Season with nutmeg, salt, and pepper. Off heat, whisk in eggs and half the parmesan.
Preheat oven to 180°C. Grease a large deep baking dish (35×25cm).
Spread half the pasta in the dish. Pour over the meat sauce. Top with remaining pasta.
Pour all the béchamel over the top, spread to edges, and sprinkle remaining parmesan.
Bake 45 minutes until top is deeply golden. Rest 15 minutes before serving.

title: Yemistá — Stuffed Bell Peppers
description: Peppers filled with spiced beef and rice, slow-baked in a rich tomato bath. A Sunday dish in Greek Cypriot homes, best eaten warm rather than piping hot.
instructions: Cut the tops off the peppers and set aside (keep them as lids). Remove seeds and membranes.
Heat 2 tbsp olive oil. Cook diced onion 5 minutes, add garlic and cook 1 more minute.
Add mince, breaking it up. Cook until just browned. Season with cinnamon, salt, and pepper.
Add rice, half the canned tomatoes, 100ml water, parsley, and mint. Stir and cook 3 minutes. The rice should be half-cooked.
Preheat oven to 180°C. Stand peppers in a deep baking dish. Fill each three-quarters full with the meat mixture (rice expands as it cooks).
Replace the pepper lids. Pour remaining tomatoes, tomato paste, 2 tbsp olive oil, and 200ml water around the peppers.
Cover with foil and bake 45 minutes. Remove foil and bake 20 more minutes until peppers are tender and sauce is reduced.
Rest 10 minutes before serving. Spoon pan juices over the peppers.
